_doc: Parameter table of the inflammatory-potential score (src/core/fii.ts): which composition signals enter it, each one's direction, weight and standardisation. Every signal is read PER 100 kcal of the pooled, cooked composition (energy-adjusted, as in the E-DII, Hébert 2019, and Food Compass, O'Hearn 2022). Standardisation is by parameter type. `corpus`: for the protective nutrients every food carries a value of, a z-score centred on the AVERAGE DIET — the global mean daily intake of Shivappa 2014 Table 2 (`dietMean`) over its global mean energy (`dietEnergyKcal`, 2,056 kcal), the energy-adjusted zero point of the E-DII — and scaled by the robust spread (IQR/1.349) of the USDA per-food densities, so a food richer than the average diet per kcal reads anti and an energy source without the nutrient (oil, sugar) reads pro by its dilution of the diet. `carrier`: one-sided, centred at 0 (absence is the baseline, never pro), each component divided by its median content among the foods that carry it and weighted by its evidence grade, so the typical carrier reads ≈ 1 unit. `limit`: one-sided pro, in multiples of the WHO intake limit expressed as a density (free sugars and saturated fat < 10 % of energy, WHO 2015 and WHO 2023; industrial trans fat < 1 %, WHO 2018; sodium < 2 g/day at a 2,000 kcal reference, WHO 2012), so a food at the limit density reads 1 unit and a dose-graded penalty replaces the narrow food-corpus scale that made every sweet or fat food saturate. Both one-sided types enter the weighted mean only at z ≥ `bonusMinZ` (0.25): absence is their baseline, and counting a zero would dilute the signals a food does carry. `weight` is the evidence grade for the direction of the parameter's effect on CRP/IL-6/TNF-α in human RCT meta-analyses (1 = consistent across markers, 0.75 = moderate, one marker, 0.5 = weak or heterogeneous, 0.25 = no RCT pool, a null pool, or a cardiometabolic proxy), not a fitted coefficient; equal weights and weights proportional to the DII overall effect scores (Shivappa 2014) are the sensitivity variants scripts/fii-sensitivity.mjs reports. Monounsaturated fat (DII −0.009), linoleic acid (Clemente-Suárez 2026) and alpha-linolenic acid (Su 2018, 25 RCTs null) are deliberately not scored; neither is retinol (vitamin A supplementation raised CRP, Gholizadeh 2022) or dietary cholesterol (egg RCTs null). `mediumChainSfaFactor` scales the 4:0–12:0 saturated fatty acids (coconut and palm-kernel lauric fat) in the saturated-fat signal: coconut oil does not raise CRP against other oils (Neelakantan 2020; Zhang 2025), while no trial isolates lauric acid, so the factor is a bounded judgment (0.25–0.5; sensitivity-tested). `pureeFreeSugarFraction` is the free-sugar fraction of fruit and vegetables whose structure is broken down (an ingredient marked `prep: blended`, purées and pastes): WHO-as-operationalised (Wanselius 2019) counts 0, UK SACN (Swan 2018) counts 1, intact cell clusters survive blending (Chu 2017) and a 16-week smoothie RCT left hs-CRP unchanged (Thomassen 2026), so a small fraction is used. `juicedFreeSugarFraction` applies to an ingredient marked `prep: juiced` (WHO: juice sugars are free). `matrixDeltas` are the composition-blind food-matrix corrections per food class (scripts/build-fii-food-classes.mjs), added to the score on the −2…+2 axis by energy share: plain dairy is neutral to beneficial in RCTs (Moosavian 2020; Nieman 2021), fermented dairy lowers CRP (Zhang 2023), and soy foods lower CRP where isolated isoflavones do not (Bajerska 2021; Gholami 2023); each direction is cited; each dairy magnitude is calibrated so the class's median food lands at its `target` (milk and cheese neutral, yogurt and kefir slightly anti, as the RCT pools read), and soy carries a fixed small credit. `minKcalPer100g` floors the dish's energy density (a near-energy-free dish such as tea is read against 20 kcal/100 g); `minCoverage` is the energy share of a dish that must report a corpus or limit parameter for it to be scored; `quorum` is the number of scored parameters at which the full ±2 range is available. `bands` are fixed edges on the score axis, symmetric about its zero point (the average diet's protective-nutrient density with no limit nutrients): neutral within ±0.3, mildly anti/pro to ±1, anti/pro beyond — so a band reads against the average diet, not against a food corpus whose vegetables would make a lentil dish look worse than typical.

parameters.cite: dietary fibre: umbrella review CRP null, TNF-α lowered (Fu 2022) — weak
vitamin C lowered IL-6 (Gholizadeh 2021) — weak to moderate
alpha-tocopherol lowered CRP across 26 RCTs, IL-6 and TNF-α null (Asbaghi 2020) — moderate
magnesium lowered CRP in 17 low-bias RCTs (Veronese 2022) — moderate
EPA + DHA lower CRP, IL-6 and TNF-α (Kavyani 2022 umbrella) — consistent
carotenoids lowered CRP across 26 RCTs, significantly for lutein/zeaxanthin and beta-cryptoxanthin; lycopene lowered IL-6 only (Hajizadeh-Sharafabad 2022) — moderate

subclass-graded: anthocyanins lowered CRP, IL-6 and TNF-α across 32 RCTs (Fallah 2020) — 1; citrus flavanones lowered CRP, GRADE moderate (Zhu 2026) — 0.75; quercetin/flavonols lowered CRP at supplement doses, I² 90 % (Tabrizi 2020) — 0.5; olive phenolics lowered CRP only against low-phenolic oil (Damasceno 2026), null across 33 RCTs (Morvaridzadeh 2024) — 0.5; flavones have no RCT meta-analysis and cocoa (Behzadi 2024) and green-tea (Haghighatdoost 2019) flavan-3-ols were null — 0.25
free sugars: SSBs raise CRP while whole fruit and 100 % juice lower or leave it (Qi 2022); honey raised IL-6 (Gonzalez 2024); unit = WHO 10 % of energy
saturated fat (Shivappa 2014), medium-chain fraction scaled by mediumChainSfaFactor; unit = WHO 10 % of energy
industrial trans fat (Valenzuela 2021); ruminant trans not scored (Radtke 2017); unit = WHO 1 % of energy
sodium, a cardiometabolic proxy: a 20-week double-blind crossover left 45 plasma cytokines unchanged (Niiranen 2023); unit = WHO 2 g/day at 2,000 kcal
